items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: The name 'Alice' is mentioned by the [INTERVIEWER] as a topic of inquiry ('And then, Alice, Alice? I've always been curious...'). The [INTERVIEWEE] responds to the question about record companies and contracts but does not mention Alice, nor does he indicate any personal interaction or relationship

ctx.x: stuff Yeah, it wasn't from here. Joe Turner. Joe Turner. So everything that we put in the bread basket was for artists away from here. And when Dick mentioned how, how played an integral part in, with the AFO record label where they were instituting the evolvement of the 50s music is right in 60, with I know that Barbara George taking and all that stuff come out right in that era right there. Well, the transition was taking place then with the R&B sound, the bass become dominant then, you know, on the recordings…

Yeah. And then, Alice, Alice? I've always been curious as to what the record companies paid the artists in the early 50s for cutting the 45. You know, what was the, and then did you sign a contract with all those people? Well, they may have signed you. Were they really open and honest about what you were signing and all that?

Well, yeah, they might be honest about what you're signing, but you never really knew what you were signing because they had some, uh, some wicked contracts. Actually, actually, what they should have said, they just put there, say, life and then sign. That's what they meant. Okay. Then, aside from that, like, ten hours a side was like the top thing.
